scope: Independent adversarial release security review of the ArrTags v1.2.0.0 release candidate: the whole candidate (secrets, authentication, state integrity, bounded-input boundaries, and the packaged artifact), focused on the surfaces v1.2 added or changed (ADR-022 through ADR-029) and on release-breadth surfaces re-verified from ADR-005 (secret boundary and version-matched leases), ADR-012 (webhook boundary), the versioned state envelope / atomic write / quarantine-vs-discard / traversal-safe path boundaries, and the bounded provider-response, webhook-body/parser, inventory-cache and configuration limits. Code claims were checked against the actual source at HEAD, not against prior reports; the recorded live pinned-host matrix (docs/implementation/21.4/live-verification.json) and the task security reviews were used as evidence where relevant. No product code, test, canonical document, or release artifact was modified; no commit was created. Reviewer-owned temporary material lives under /tmp/final-review/security/21.5/.

findings.area: secret / provider transport boundary (credential forwarded across an HTTP redirect)
findings.summary: NEW finding, not a v1.2 regression and not present in any prior review. The provider clients are registered with a bare AddHttpClient(name) and therefore inherit the .NET default AllowAutoRedirect=true; the shared-secret X-Api-Key header applied by SecretLease.ApplyTo is re-sent by the handler to whatever origin a 3xx Location names. Reproduced end to end against the exact DI shape ArrTagsServiceRegistrator builds: a listener on the configured provider origin answered 302 with Location: http://127.0.0.1:18099/collect and the second origin received 'X-Api-Key=SUPER-SECRET-API-KEY-VALUE'. ADR-005 requires the key to be sent 'only as X-Api-Key' for 'the current request only' and confines it to 'the outbound authenticated request while it is being sent'; a redirect hop is a different origin and a different request, so the shipped behavior widens the credential's egress beyond the configured connection. Impact is a real credential-disclosure path, not an unbounded-work or memory issue, and it is not remotely triggerable by an unauthenticated third party against the Jellyfin host: the configured base URL is administrator-supplied, and the redirect has to come from that configured provider (or from a network position already able to observe the key, at which point the plugin's behavior is not the weak link). That is why this is MEDIUM and not HIGH, and it is recorded as open rather than being waved through as hardening.
evidence: src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:215-226 (RegisterProviderHttpClients: bare serviceCollection.AddHttpClient(ArrHttpClientNames.Sonarr/Radarr) and only the two AllowInsecure names get ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler; no AllowAutoRedirect=false and no MaxAutomaticRedirections=0 on any of the four clients, and no handler override that would set them)
src/ArrTags/Providers/ArrHttpClientFactory.cs:32-53 (CreateClient only sets BaseAddress, Timeout and Accept; it never constrains redirect behaviour, so the factory default applies)
src/ArrTags/Secrets/SecretLease.cs:46-58 (ApplyTo adds the key to the shared HttpRequestMessage; a redirect hop clones the request, so the header is carried)

src/ArrTags/Providers/Sonarr/SonarrClient.cs:287-288 and src/ArrTags/Providers/Radarr/RadarrClient.cs:261-262 (HttpMethod.Get + lease.ApplyTo(request) on every attempt; the read path is the only place a lease is applied to an outbound request)

reproduction /tmp/final-review/security/21.5/redirect (standalone net10.0 program using the identical 'new ServiceCollection().AddHttpClient("sonarr")' registration, an HttpListener provider origin on 127.0.0.1:18098 answering 302 Location: http://127.0.0.1:18099/collect, and a second HttpListener on 127.0.0.1:18099): output 'PROVIDER-ORIGIN(18098) got: GET /api/v3/system/status  X-Api-Key=SUPER-SECRET-API-KEY-VALUE' then 'REDIRECT-TARGET(127.0.0.1:18099) RECEIVED: GET http://127.0.0.1:18099/collect  X-Api-Key=SUPER-SECRET-API-KEY-VALUE' with final status 200

docs/decisions/ADR-005.md:51 ('add X-Api-Key to the current request only') and :111 ('The API key is sent only as X-Api-Key; query-string authentication is not permitted') — the decision constrains transport, not redirect scope, so the gap is in the implementation against the accepted decision

docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 2.4 ('A plugin should configure the behavior it requires on its own named or typed client'), which makes the omission a plugin-side choice rather than a host contract

scope check: grep src/ArrTags for AllowAutoRedirect|MaxAutomaticRedirections|ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler returns only the two CreateInsecureHandler lines, and grep for HttpMethod.|new HttpRequestMessage returns only HttpMethod.Get in SonarrClient.cs:287 and RadarrClient.cs:261, so the provider integration remains read-only and the redirect behaviour is uniform across both providers
findings.recommended_action: Constrain the redirect behaviour the plugin actually requires on its own four named clients, which is what the pinned-host research already prescribes: in RegisterProviderHttpClients, set .ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler(() => new SocketsHttpHandler { AllowAutoRedirect = false }) (or MaxAutomaticRedirections = 0) for the strict Sonarr/Radarr names, and add the same setting to the existing CreateInsecureHandler so the opt-in TLS relaxation does not also change credential scope. A provider that legitimately needs a redirect can be handled explicitly rather than by following it. Add a transport test that asserts a 302 from the configured origin is not followed with the key attached, and record the decision (or an explicit accepted limitation) in ADR-005.

findings.summary: Carried unchanged from the task-15.4 review (SR-15.4-01) and re-verified at HEAD, not a v1.2 regression. Control-scalar removal in LogSubject.NormalizeFileName is Unicode Cc only (Rune.IsControl), so every other non-printing scalar a media file name can carry reaches the operator-facing log verbatim: Cf format characters (U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE, U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE, U+2066/U+2069 LRI/PDI, U+00AD, U+FEFF) and the Zl/Zp separators U+2028/U+2029. Reproduced end to end against the shipped Release assembly. This is a log-integrity and readability weakness with no secret exposure and no volume amplification: the throttle keys on category plus the code-owned ArrTagsLogEvent and never on the message or subject, and the subject is bounded to 128 scalars, so a hostile file name cannot grow the tracking set or the log volume. Kept LOW and open as optional hardening rather than closed, because it was adjudicated as such twice already and nothing in v1.2 changed it.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs:78-102 (NormalizeFileName skips only Rune.IsControl(rune) scalars; every other rune is appended verbatim up to MaximumScalarValues=128)

reproduction against /workspace/ArrTags/src/ArrTags/bin/Release/net10.0/ArrTags.dll (probe at /tmp/final-review/security/21.5/probe2): '/m/Movie\u202Egpj.mkv' -> 'Movie\u202Egpj.mkv' (U+202E present); '/m/Movie\u200Bb.mkv' -> U+200B present; '/m/Movie\u2066x\u2069.mkv' -> U+2066 and U+2069 present; '/m/Movie\u2028b.mkv' -> U+2028 present; '/m/Movie\u2029b.mkv' -> U+2029 present; control case '/m/Movie\u0001b.mkv' -> 'Movieb.mkv' (correctly stripped), so the bound is Cc-only and not broken

volume bound unchanged: src/ArrTags/Logging/LogThrottle.cs:63-107 keys admission on category + logEvent only and caps the tracking set at MaxTrackedKeys=256, so the subject cannot be used to evade or amplify the ADR-020 clause 6 bound
carried from docs/implementation/15.4/security-review.json finding SR-15.4-01 (LOW, open) and restated in the ADR-026 implementation note in docs/decisions/ADR-026.md

no secret reaches the subject: the fallback is the item identifier and the primary source is a media path, so a secret cannot enter through this helper; docs/decisions/ADR-026.md clause 4 keeps the secret-exclusion set unchanged
findings.recommended_action: Optional hardening, not a release gate: extend the removal predicate in NormalizeFileName to also drop non-printing/format scalars (at minimum the Cf category and U+2028/U+2029), or normalize them to a visible placeholder. If the literal 'control characters' reading of ADR-026 clause 2 is kept, record the Cf/Zl/Zp pass-through as an accepted limitation in docs/limitations/accepted.md rather than only in the task-15.4 review.

findings.area: log path disclosure / bounded log subject (ADR-026)
findings.summary: Carried unchanged from the task-15.4 review (SR-15.4-02) and re-verified at HEAD, not a v1.2 regression. Path.GetFileName uses host-platform separator semantics, so on the pinned Linux host a backslash is a legal file-name character: a Windows-style primary path is emitted whole, disclosing a user account name and a full directory chain in the log subject, contrary to the explicit directory/full-path exclusion ADR-026 added. Reproduced against the shipped Release assembly. The exposure is bounded (a real Jellyfin media path on the pinned Linux host cannot carry a backslash) and no secret is involved, so this stays LOW. The related SR-15.4-04 observation (Path.GetFileName is a path splitter, not a URL parser, so a URL-shaped primary path keeps its query string) was re-checked and is unreachable for a Jellyfin media path, which is why it is folded into this finding rather than raised separately.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs:47-68 (Create calls Path.GetFileName(primaryPath) with no host-platform normalization)

reproduction against the shipped Release assembly: 'C:\Users\admin\Videos\secret.mkv' -> subject 'C:\Users\admin\Videos\secret.mkv' (32 scalars, user name and full path disclosed); '\\fileserver\media\secret\file.mkv' -> emitted whole (34 scalars, share server and path disclosed)

positive controls in the same run confirm the normal POSIX contract holds: '/media/movies/Example.mkv' -> 'Example.mkv'; '/srv/media/4K Movies/Some.Movie.2019.mkv' -> 'Some.Movie.2019.mkv'; a 300-character name is truncated to exactly 128 scalars

ADR-026 implementation note in docs/decisions/ADR-026.md records the same host-native-path reading; the ADR-026 clause 1 directory/full-path exclusion is therefore not enforced for a Windows-style value on a POSIX host
carried from docs/implementation/15.4/security-review.json finding SR-15.4-02 (LOW, open)
findings.recommended_action: Optional hardening: split on both '/' and '\\' in LogSubject.Create before taking the file-name component (and re-run the fallback check afterwards), so the ADR-026 clause 1 directory/full-path exclusion holds regardless of which separator the host-native path uses. Add the two Windows/UNC cases to LogSubjectTests as explicit cases rather than relying on the host default.

findings.summary: Carried unchanged from the 0.1.0 final review (SEC-2) and re-verified at HEAD, not a v1.2 regression. When IPluginManager is unavailable or the loaded plugin instance cannot be found, CreateStateRepository roots the entire authoritative plugin state at Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "ArrTags") — a predictable, shared local path another local user could pre-create or observe. Not triggered on the pinned host (the plugin is found and DataFolderPath is the relocated ProgramDataPath/ArrTags root), and not remotely reachable. Not a release blocker; recorded again so the v1.2 release carries it forward honestly rather than silently dropping it.
evidence: src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:269-278 (string.IsNullOrEmpty(plugin?.DataFolderPath) ? Path.Combine(Path.GetTempPath(), "ArrTags") : plugin!.DataFolderPath)

src/ArrTags/Plugin.cs:65-66 and :269-273 show the normal path re-points DataFolderPath at ResolveStateRootDirectory (ProgramDataPath/ArrTags) via SetAttributes before any state is written, so the fallback is not taken on the pinned host

docs/implementation/21.4/live-verification.json L8 observed the relocated root at /tmp/arrtags-21.4/data/ArrTags (26 files across artifacts/source, authoritative/{artwork-operation,artwork-state,source-artifact}, cache/{metadata-state,reconciliation-cursor}) and confirmed it is removed on uninstall, i.e. the shared-temp fallback was not used
carried from docs/implementation/final-review/security-review.json SEC-2 (LOW, open) and registered in docs/limitations/00-index.md
findings.recommended_action: Fail closed (do not register the state-dependent services) or resolve a host-private per-user directory when the plugin data folder cannot be resolved, instead of a shared temp path. Cheap to fix and worth doing before a future release that touches registration.

findings.area: secret boundary / state envelope integrity scope
findings.summary: Carried unchanged (0.1.0 SEC-3 / 14.4 SEC-14.4-06) and re-verified at HEAD. The versioned state envelope's SHA-256 covers only PayloadJson; SchemaVersion, Kind, RecordId, Authority, Terminal and UpdatedUtc are not covered, and authoritative retention trusts the unauthenticated Terminal/UpdatedUtc fields. Not an escalation: local write access to the state root is already the administrative boundary and such a writer could delete files directly, so the guarantee is corruption detection rather than tamper authentication. This is the same integrity model the v1.2 reconciliation cursor relies on (ADR-022 clause 4 / ADR-029 keep the existing envelope shape unchanged), so it is a property of the release-breadth state boundary rather than a v1.2 change.
evidence: src/ArrTags/State/StateEnvelopeCodec.cs:83-113 (the hash is compared only against parsed.PayloadJson) and :123-154 (TryReadEnvelope validates only SchemaVersion before the payload hash check)
src/ArrTags/State/StateRetention.cs:154-165 (IsTerminalAndExpired reads envelope.Terminal and envelope.UpdatedUtc without an integrity-covered value)

src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/ReconciliationCursorStore.cs:62-101 shows the v1.2 cursor is subject to the same envelope integrity contract and treats a failed check as a miss (Cache authority), so a torn or tampered cursor resets to the start rather than being trusted
findings.recommended_action: None required for this release. Optionally cover the envelope metadata in the integrity hash, or document StateEnvelopeCodec explicitly as a corruption detector rather than a tamper MAC, so a future reader does not over-read the guarantee.

findings.area: bounded input / configuration limits (v1.2 byte-limit conversion, ADR-028)
findings.summary: Positive confirmation plus a documented bound, verified against the shipped code rather than the page. The server-side OperationalLimits.Validate enforces the documented byte range for all seven byte-denominated limits (ProviderResponseLimitBytes 64 KiB..64 MiB, WebhookMaxPayloadBytes 4 KiB..4 MiB, and the rest per the ADR-028 table), and an over-max or under-min candidate is rejected, so a raw API POST cannot widen a limit. The step-multiple rejection is page-side only, exactly as ADR-028 clause 1 specifies and as the live verifier already recorded (F-21.4-4), so an off-step in-range value is accepted by the API. That is the documented design, not a defect, and it is already registered as V12-G6-1 / F-21.4-4. No secret is exposed by the conversion, and a saved value cannot inject into a URL, a filesystem path, a fingerprint, or a log line: the page converts to a bounded integer, the server re-validates the byte range, and the persisted value stays bytes.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Configuration/OperationalLimits.cs:171-204 (Validate enforces the byte range for every byte-denominated field; the step is deliberately not enforced here)
src/ArrTags/Configuration/ByteLimitUnits.cs:21-86 and src/ArrTags/Configuration/ByteLimitField.cs (code-owned unit/step/precision per field; the page mirror at config.html:322-330 matches)

reproduction: OperationalLimits.Validate accepts 65536 (min), 67108864 (max), 1572865 (off-step but in range) and 100000 (legacy in-range off-step), and rejects 65535, 67108865 and 1024; PluginConfigurationValidator.Validate on a configuration carrying ProviderResponseLimitBytes=1572865 returns IsValid=true, confirming the range check is what actually gates a save

src/ArrTags/Configuration/config.html:397-437 (byteLimitToBytes rejects any value that is not an exact step multiple and returns null, which aborts the submit before the POST; readByteLimitValues never sends a partial set)

docs/decisions/ADR-028.md clause 1 ('the settings conversion/validation path ... must add an explicit step check. The internal OperationalLimits byte-range validation is unchanged'); docs/implementation/21.4/live-verification.json F-21.4-4 and docs/limitations/00-index.md V12-G6-1 record the same bound
findings.recommended_action: None required. Keep the page-side step check and the server-side range check as they are, and keep the V12-G6-1 / F-21.4-4 wording so no future claim implies the API enforces step alignment.

findings.area: bounded input / persisted reconciliation cursor (ADR-022, ADR-029, v1.2)
findings.summary: Positive confirmation of the v1.2 cursor's state-integrity and bounded-input properties, verified by direct exercise of the shipped store. The cursor is a single fixed-kind, fixed-id, versioned, integrity-checked Cache-authority record; it carries only the bounded scope identity and the opaque (SortName, itemId) position, never a path, provider payload or credential; it fails closed to a miss (reset to the start) rather than being quarantined or trusted; and the record id and kind are fixed code constants, so no attacker-influenced value reaches a filesystem path. The write is bounded and the read is bounded by the documented 4,096 library-id and 256-character library-id-length caps. Two honest observations: (a) the scope identity is built from snapshot.EnabledLibraries, which the configuration validator does not count- or length-bound (the carried SEC-11 / SEC-14.4-02 LOW), so a pathological saved configuration makes every cursor write throw ArgumentException inside ReconciliationCursorStore.Write — the throw is contained by LibraryReconciliationService.AdvanceCursor, so the run completes and the cursor simply never persists (coverage degrades to the pre-v1.2 prefix behaviour, not a failure); and (b) the SortName hint is truncated to 512 characters on write and is a hint only, never the ordering authority, so it cannot widen the resume or the record.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/ReconciliationCursorStore.cs:26-31 (fixed RecordKind 'reconciliation-cursor' and fixed RecordId 'current'), :55-101 (read treats a failed envelope check, a failed semantic Validate or a scope mismatch as a miss/reset; TryDiscard deletes the cache record), :113-133 (write validates before writing and never writes a partially valid record), :135-140 (BoundSortName truncates to 512)

src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/ReconciliationCursor.cs:24-41 (CurrentCursorVersion=1, MaxEnabledLibraryIds=4096, MaxEnabledLibraryIdLength=256, MaxSortNameHintLength=512) and :111-156 (Validate rejects an incompatible version, too many ids, a blank/over-long id, an empty anchor id, and a SortName-without-position record)

src/ArrTags/State/PluginStatePaths.cs:64-103 (GetRecordPath validates both segments as single path segments: '..', '../evil', 'a/b' and '/abs' are all rejected with ArgumentException in the reproduction, and a 201-character segment is rejected by the 200-character cap)

src/ArrTags/Reconciliation/LibraryReconciliationService.cs:151-152 (the cursor governs only Scheduled and PostScan), :418-437 (AdvanceCursor contains every write failure and never fails the run), :173-183 (an unlocatable anchor resets to the start rather than failing the run, ADR-029 clause 4)

reproduction: a 3-library scope writes and reads back Position @11111111-...; a 5,000-library scope and a 300-character single library id both throw ArgumentException from Write and the subsequent Read reports ScopeChanged (a miss), with the previously written record left intact on disk; the persisted envelope is {"SchemaVersion":1,"Kind":"reconciliation-cursor","RecordId":"current","Authority":0,...,"PayloadJson":"{\"CursorVersion\":1,\"EnabledLibraryIds\":[...],\"MoviePosters\":true,\"EpisodePosters\":true,\"SortName\":\"Some Movie (2020)\",\"ItemId\":\"...\"}"} — no path, no provider payload, no credential
tests/ArrTags.Tests/ReconciliationCursorStoreTests.cs and ReconciliationCursorResumeTests.cs run in the default suite (Failed 0, Passed 1,927, Skipped 66, Total 1,993)
findings.recommended_action: None required. If SEC-11 (unbounded EnabledLibraries) is ever fixed, re-check that the cursor's 4,096-entry cap is compatible with the chosen validator bound so the containment path in AdvanceCursor is not the normal path.

findings.summary: Positive confirmation of the v1.2 diagnostics surface. ArrTagsStatusController is class-level [Authorize(Policy = Policies.RequiresElevation)] with [ApiController] and [Route("ArrTags/Status")], exactly one [HttpGet] action, no [AllowAnonymous] at class or action level, and no write verb, second route, or configuration setting; it returns the fixed-shape DiagnosticsSnapshot unchanged and performs no provider, render, library or I/O work. The snapshot is 9 top-level fields of counts and bounded enums with no per-item array, and the panel renders only from that fixed set using textContent (no innerHTML/outerHTML/document.write/eval/insertAdjacentHTML anywhere in config.html), only a count after a typeof/isFinite check and only a health value from the declared ArrConnectionHealth names, so a free-form response string can never be rendered. The panel is static-hidden and empty until a bounded snapshot renders and clears on a rejected, unavailable or non-object response, and the page resource itself holds no secret literal (the only occurrence of the word 'secret' is the descriptive help text for the webhook header). Live confirmation: anonymous GET /ArrTags/Status -> 401 with an empty body, admin GET -> the documented fixed shape, admin POST/DELETE -> 405, and a sibling /ArrTags/Stats -> 404.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Diagnostics/ArrTagsStatusController.cs:27-59 (class-level [Authorize(Policy = Policies.RequiresElevation)], [Route(RoutePrefix)] with RoutePrefix='ArrTags/Status', one [HttpGet] returning _snapshotProvider.GetSnapshot() unchanged; the constructor null-checks its single dependency)
src/ArrTags/Diagnostics/DiagnosticsSnapshotProvider.cs:45-48 (GetSnapshot only reads the in-memory counters plus the queue's bounded Count/InFlightCount; no lock, I/O or work)

src/ArrTags/Diagnostics/DiagnosticsMetrics.cs:140-200 (Capture copies counters only; the render-failure array is sized by the declared RenderFailureReason enum and out-of-range values are ignored) and :107-121 (provider health is written into a fixed array sized by ArrProviderKind and rejects undefined values)

src/ArrTags/Configuration/config.html:520-549 (fixed 28-entry counter table, all code-owned labels), :569-594 (a count renders only after typeof 'number' && isFinite, a health only from the five declared names, otherwise 'Unknown'), :596-643 (renders with textContent only; a null, array, string or number response leaves the panel cleared and hidden), :645-664 (one GET per page show, no retry or polling, clears on rejection)
grep src/ArrTags/Configuration/config.html for innerHTML|outerHTML|document.write|eval(|new Function|insertAdjacentHTML|.src=|location. -> no matches

docs/implementation/21.4/live-verification.json L5: anonymous 401 (empty body) with and without an Authorization header, admin 200 with the 9-field/28-leaf fixed shape and 0 '[' characters, admin POST 405, admin DELETE 405, /ArrTags/Stats 404, and a secret/payload/path regex scan over the body returning 0 matches

artifact check: the embedded resource ArrTags.Configuration.config.html extracted from the shipped ArrTags.dll is byte-identical to src/ArrTags/Configuration/config.html, so the reviewed page is the served page
findings.recommended_action: None required. The one standing bound is the already-registered V12-F3-1 / SR-17.4-02: the panel's inline JavaScript is never executed by the suite or the documented live matrix (no JavaScript runtime; the pinned host runs --nowebclient), so the panel behaviour is pinned structurally against the endpoint model rather than executed. Keep that qualifier on any future claim about the panel.

findings.summary: Positive confirmation, re-verified against the shipped source rather than trusting the prior audits. The pre-binding WebhookAuthenticationFilter is still an IAsyncAuthorizationFilter applied with [TypeFilter(...)] on the [AllowAnonymous] ArrTagsWebhookController, so MVC authenticates before model binding and no request body is read for any content type; it then rejects a declared non-JSON content type with a bounded 400 before the read, and the action independently re-authenticates and applies the configured WebhookMaxPayloadBytes bound. WebhookAuthentication.Authenticate fails closed with a distinct internal result for NotConfigured, MissingCredential and Mismatch but the controller and the filter map all three to the same status, and a candidate longer than 1024 characters is rejected before any comparison or allocation proportional to it; the comparison itself is CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals. Provider errors are bounded code-owned strings (ArrProviderError.Message is trimmed and truncated to 512 characters and every producer is a fixed literal, never a response body or header), and no secret, header or body is reflected. The provider integration remains read-only: the only HttpRequestMessage construction in the whole source uses HttpMethod.Get.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Webhooks/WebhookAuthenticationFilter.cs:32-101 (IAsyncAuthorizationFilter authenticates first and returns UnauthorizedResult before any body read, then rejects a non-JSON content type with BadRequestResult before binding; only a fixed bounded reason string is logged)

summary: Independent adversarial release security review of the ArrTags v1.2.0.0 release candidate (reviewed HEAD e172c4c; artifact artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip, 619,538 bytes, SHA-256 505804992a50d7aa073b07cfaa8dc0c8ac9a95041a7c394d8bd54dd959f90762, 7 entries, no SkiaSharp.dll or libSkiaSharp.so). reviewer_status PASS_WITH_FINDINGS with open_blocker_high = 0: no open BLOCKER and no open HIGH, so the task 21.5 acceptance criterion is met. One new MEDIUM finding is recorded. SEC-21.5-01: the provider clients are registered with a bare AddHttpClient(name) and therefore inherit the .NET default redirect-following, and the X-Api-Key header applied by SecretLease.ApplyTo is re-sent to whatever origin a 3xx Location names; I reproduced this end to end with the exact DI shape ArrTagsServiceRegistrator builds, and it widens the credential's egress beyond the configured connection relative to ADR-005's 'the current request only' requirement. It is MEDIUM rather than HIGH because it is not reachable by an unauthenticated third party against the Jellyfin host — the base URL is administrator-supplied and the redirect must originate from the configured provider or from a network position that can already read the key — and it is a small, well-understood fix. Three LOW findings are carried forward honestly and re-verified at HEAD rather than closed: the Cc-only control removal in the bounded log subject (SEC-21.5-02, reproduced), the POSIX host treating a backslash as a file-name character and so emitting a Windows or UNC path whole (SEC-21.5-03, reproduced), and the shared-temp-path state-root fallback (SEC-21.5-04, unreachable on the pinned host). The v1.2 additions themselves hold up under adversarial checking. The ADR-025 diagnostics endpoint is class-level elevation-gated with a single read-only GET, a fixed 9-field/28-leaf count-and-enum shape, and a panel that renders only through textContent from that fixed set, fails closed, and holds no secret or data. The ADR-026 bounded subject never carries a directory, full path or secret on a native path, is bounded to 128 scalars, and cannot be used to evade or amplify the log-volume bound because the throttle never keys on the message. The ADR-028 conversion fails closed on a non-step value, aborts the submit before any partial POST, and the server independently enforces the byte range, so a saved configuration cannot widen a limit or inject into a URL, path, fingerprint or log line. The ADR-022/ADR-029 cursor is a fixed-kind, fixed-id, versioned, integrity-checked Cache record that carries only a bounded scope identity and an opaque (SortName, itemId) anchor, resets rather than trusting an invalid or unlocatable position, and whose write failure is contained. The ADR-023 re-enqueue is issued after the in-flight slot is released and is bounded to one per (item, connection, surface, version), so it cannot loop. The ADR-024 restore runs only through the single guarded, crash-recoverable publisher entry point under a durable fence, and every other pass-through reason still preserves the current artwork. The provider integration remains GET-only, secrets are contained to the configuration, the private snapshot, a short-lived lease and the outbound header, and the shipped assembly is byte-identical to a clean build of the audited source. The default suite is Failed 0, Passed 1,927, Skipped 66, Total 1,993 and the security-focused subset is Failed 0, Passed 316, Skipped 1, Total 317. The standing accepted limitations (D1, D2, SEC-9 through SEC-12, V12-G6-1, V12-G8-1, V12-G8-2, V12-F3-1, V12-F4-1 through V12-F4-6, V12-F6-1, V12-F6-2) were each re-checked against the code and remain accurate; none was silently dropped. The one recommended action before or shortly after release is SEC-21.5-01: constrain the redirect behaviour on the plugin's four named Arr HTTP clients.
